 Order

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 (1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is arising out of award dated 08.04.2008 passed by Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mhow, District - Indore (MP) in Claim Case No.96 of 2006 on account of exonerating him from compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mhow, District - Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: (2) The brief facts of the case are that on 26.03.2006 at about 8.15 pm, the deceased was going on his motorcycle bearing registration No.MP09LA-7485 from Biyani Automobiles to his house at Badgonda, then as soon as he reached near Kalal Ghati, the driver of one motorcycle Hero Honda Passion No.MP09LJ- 9751, respondent No.6 while driving the said vehicle rashly and negligently dashed the deceased Rajendra, as a result, of which the deceased sustained grievous injuries on his person and grievous injuries on head and other parts of the body and he died during the treatment.

(3) The claimants/respondents No.1 to 5, being the legal representatives of deceased Rajendra had filed a claim application under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, against the appellant and rest of the respondents, before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mhow, District-Indore for compensation of Rs.26,95,000/-.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mhow, District-Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: (4) The appellant contested the claim and have denied all the material allegations.
The other respondents were proceeded ex parte before the Claims Tribunal.

(5) The Claims Tribunal after framing the issues and after recording evidence of both the parties has allowed the claim of respondent No.1 to 5 and has awarded Rs.3,46,100/- in their favour and against the appellant.

(6) Counsel for the appellant has filed this appeal on the ground that the impugned award is bad in law and not borne out from the facts, evidence and material on record and is liable to be set-aside.
He further submits that injuries sustained by him is due to slipping of vehicle which he himself was driving.

The Tribunal has grossly erred in not considering the fact that in medical record in Ex.D/1,
it was mentioned that the deceased was injured due to slipping of his vehicle which has been recorded in the hospital record.
He further submitted that at the time of accident, the driver of offending vehicle was not having the valid driving licence so it is a breach of insurance policy.
Hence prays for exonerating the Insurance Company from liability.

(7) Counsel for the respondents/claimants for allowing the appeal and has supported the impugned award in this regard and has also filed the cross objection under Order 41 Rule 22 of CPC for seeking enhancement of compensation and submitted that Tribunal has committed error in assessing the income of deceased.
He has filed the income certificate as Ex.P/12 which was proved by the claimants witnesses and hence prays for enhancement of compensation.

(8) Counsel for the Insurance Company prays for dismissing the cross-objection.
(9) On perusal of the record, it was found that in Ex.D/1, it was mentioned in Page 85 that accident occurred due to slip of vehicle.
This document was exhibited by the Insurance Company before the Claims Tribunal but the Insurance Company was unable to adduce any witness who wrote this note in Ex.D/1.
(10) Counsel for the appellant submitted that the document was exhibited by the Court but it is an inadmissible document.
It is stated that admissibility of document is one thing and authenticity is another thing.
The document so exhibited by the Court does not mean that this document is admissible in the eyes of law.

It is the duty of Insurance Company to adduce the evidence of Doctor who wrote the note in Ex.D/1 that the friend who was the pillion rider has stated that due to slip of kinetic scooter the deceased has received the injuries but the Insurance Company has unable to adduce any evidence in the Court so this note was appropriately proved by the Insurance Company and hence this document was not admissible in the eyes of law and in view of lack of evidence it was not proved that accident occurred due to slip of kinetic scooter.
So the arguments put-forth by the Insurance Company has no substance.
Counsel for the Insurance Company has argued that at the time of accident, the driver of offending vehicle has no valid or effective driving licence so this argument has no substance.
Hence the appeal filed by the Insurance Company has no substance and is liable to be dismissed.
(11) On the other hand, counsel for the respondents/claimants has submitted that the deceased was working as Store Keeper and Supervisor in Biyani Automobiles and used to earn Rs.5000/- per month.
He filed Ex.D/12 as payslip of the deceased.
Mr. Dhirendra Singh AW/6 has stated in evidence that the deceased was working as Supervisor in Biyani Automobiles Showroom and he used to get Rs.5000/- per month as salary.

He admitted in cross-examination that no attendance register was produced before the Tribunal and no record of Automobile Showroom as regards payment of deceased was shown before the Tribunal as per para 37 and 38 of judgment.

(12) In the considered opinion of this Court, the Tribunal has rightly rejected the income of deceased as Rs.5000/- per month and as per Labour Commissioner Report, the unskilled labour gets Rs.2694/- per month and hence the compensation must be assessed on the basis of Minimum Wages Act.
In view of this Court, the just and proper income of the deceased is Rs.2694/- per month.

(13) After hearing counsel for the parties and on perusal of the evidence on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the Tribunal has erred in assessing the income of the deceased considering the record and documents.

Hence, in the considered opinion of this Court, the compensation deserves to be enhanced in the following manner:-
Loss of Dependency Rs.2694/-+Rs.1077(40%FP)=Rs.3771/-(less1/3)
Rs.1257/-=Rs.2514x12x17=Rs.5,12,856/-
 Funeral Expenses Rs.15000/-
 Loss of Estate Rs.15000/-

(14) Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.5,42,856/- as against the award of Tribunal of Rs.3,46,100/-.
Accordingly, the respondents/claimants are entitled to get an additional sum of Rs.1,96,756/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
(15) Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellant-Insurance Company is dismissed.
The cross-objection is allowed in part to the extent indicated herein above.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
